title: ShareInviteListResponse
description: Envelope returned by GET /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites — the owner's invite list for one vehicle (MYR-184 vehicle-sharing self-serve). Wraps the rows under `invites` (NOT the `items` key used by the paginated list envelopes VehicleListResponse / DrivesListResponse / RideRequestsListResponse): this surface is deliberately UNPAGINATED — an owner's per-vehicle invite set is small and bounded, there is no cursor and no `hasMore`, and naming the key `invites` keeps it from being mistaken for a page of a cursor-paginated collection by an SDK pagination helper. The envelope itself is part of the wire contract: consumers MUST NOT strip it silently. Sharing is Go-owned end to end (table `go_vehicle_shares`, no FKs to Prisma tables, CG-DL-9); the email-keyed Prisma `Invite` table is retired unused, and this schema amends rest-api.md DV-23, which had assigned invites to the now-deprecated Next.js app. Single-resource endpoints in this family return a bare ShareInvite from `$defs`: POST /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites (create), POST /api/invites/{inviteId}/resend (new code + reset expiry), and — as of MYR-369 — PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId} (edit one ACCEPTED grant's capabilities in place, body PatchShareInviteRequest). DELETE /api/invites/{inviteId} (cancel a pending invite or revoke an accepted grant) returns no body. As of MYR-609 a fifth single-resource route joins them: POST /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/share/extend (body ExtendShareRequest) copies one of the owner's ACCEPTED grants onto another car they own and returns the new accepted ShareInvite with 201.

invites.description: Invite rows for the path vehicle that the calling OWNER may see. Always present; an empty array (never null) means this vehicle has no pending invites and no accepted viewers. Order is server-defined (currently newest first, ORDER BY created_at DESC). REVOKED rows are NEVER serialized: revocation is a tombstone flip in `go_vehicle_shares` (status 'revoked', not a delete) kept server-side for audit, and the wire status enum has no 'revoked' member — a revoked row simply disappears from this list. Drives the owner's sharing screen, which splits these rows into its two sections by `status`: accepted rows render under 'Viewers · N' and pending rows under 'Pending' (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx InvitesScreen, jsx:1296-1330).

SharePermission.description: INVITE-TIME PRESET, and — on an accepted row — a DERIVED COMPATIBILITY PROJECTION of the per-grant capability flags. NO LONGER A CUMULATIVE TIER (MYR-369). Read the two lives of this value separately, because they are no longer the same thing. (1) ON A PENDING INVITE it is the preset the owner chose in the send-invite sheet, carried on the row until redemption, at which point the server MAPS it onto the accepted grant's flags: 'rides' → allowRides true, everything else → allowRides false. That mapping is the ONLY thing the preset does; after redemption the flags are authoritative and the preset is inert. (2) ON AN ACCEPTED GRANT it is DERIVED FROM THE FLAGS on every read — allowRides true → 'rides', otherwise 'live' — so it is a lossy projection kept for pre-MYR-369 clients, never a stored tier and never something to write. A consumer that wants the truth reads `allowRides` and `suspended`; a consumer that only understands this enum still gets a correct coarse answer. WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. Before MYR-369 the three members formed a total order (live < live_history < rides) that consumers compared with >=, and a grant's tier was fixed for its life. It is now a SET OF INDEPENDENT, EDITABLE PER-GRANT CAPABILITIES (see ShareInvite.allowRides / ShareInvite.suspended), so the >= comparison is WRONG on an accepted row and MUST be replaced by a direct read of the flags. 'live_history' IS RETIRED AND IS NEVER EMITTED. It stays in this enum for wire compatibility only — an installed client that still has it in its decoder keeps decoding — but no server response carries it on any surface as of MYR-369, and no accepted grant derives it. The capability it named (the drives / trip-history surfaces for a non-owner) has been REMOVED FROM THE PRODUCT: those endpoints are owner-only again, unconditionally, and a legacy grant created at the 'live_history' preset now derives 'live' and reads drives no more than a 'live' grant does. CreateShareInviteRequest still ACCEPTS 'live_history' so an old client's send-invite sheet does not start failing, but the server PERSISTS it as 'live'. Consumers MUST NOT introduce new uses of the member and SHOULD treat it, if one is ever decoded from an old persisted payload, as exactly equivalent to 'live'. Swift consumers get the decode-tolerant unrecognized(String) catch-all via codegen (MYR-195), so neither the retirement nor a future member breaks installed clients.

PatchShareInviteRequest.title: PatchShareInviteRequest
PatchShareInviteRequest.description: Request body for PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId} — the owner editing ONE accepted grant's capabilities in place (MYR-369). This endpoint is what replaces the pre-MYR-369 rule that a grant's access was fixed for its life and changing it meant revoke-plus-reinvite. ACCEPTED GRANTS ONLY: an invite still `pending` is rejected 409 `conflict`, because a pending row has no grant to edit — its access is decided at redemption from the invite's `permission` preset, so an owner who wants different terms cancels it and sends a new one. PARTIAL BY DESIGN: every property is optional and only the properties PRESENT are written; an absent property leaves that capability exactly as it was, and is NOT the same as sending `false`. At least one property is required (`minProperties: 1`) — an empty body is 400 `invalid_request` rather than a no-op, so a client bug cannot look like a successful edit. OWNER-ONLY, and an invite that does not exist, belongs to another owner, or is a revoked tombstone all answer 404 `not_found` INDISTINGUISHABLY — the same non-oracle rule DELETE and resend follow, so this endpoint cannot be used to probe for other people's invite ids. The 200 response is the updated `ShareInvite` (an accepted row, so it carries `allowRides`, `suspended` and the derived `permission`, and carries neither `code` nor `shareUrl`). Applies to ONE ROW: a multi-vehicle invite is N rows, and patching one changes that vehicle's grant only, so an owner may hold different capabilities per vehicle for the same person — which the fixed pre-MYR-369 tier could not express.

allowRides.description: Set the grant's ride-request capability — see ShareInvite.allowRides. Omit to leave it unchanged. Setting it true does NOT un-suspend: a suspended grant with allowRides true still cannot request a ride, because suspension gates everything (see ShareInvite.suspended). Setting it false takes effect on the next request the viewer makes; it does NOT cancel ride requests they have already had accepted.

suspended.description: Suspend (true) or restore (false) the whole grant — see ShareInvite.suspended. Omit to leave it unchanged. TRUE IS THE BIG HAMMER: it removes the vehicle from the viewer's access set entirely, so their catalog row, snapshot, WebSocket subscription, drives and rides all stop at once, while the grant row survives so a later `false` restores exactly the capabilities it had. It is the reversible alternative to DELETE (revoke), which is a permanent tombstone the viewer can only get back through a fresh invite.

ExtendShareRequest.title: ExtendShareRequest
ExtendShareRequest.description: Request body for POST /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/share/extend — the owner copying one of their ACCEPTED grants onto another car they own, in one call (MYR-609, rest-api.md §7.5.8). It is the only endpoint in this family that produces an accepted grant WITHOUT the grantee performing an act, and the consent basis is narrow: the grantee already accepted a share FROM THIS OWNER, both the source grant and the target car must belong to the CALLER (checked in SQL on both halves, so this can never reach across owners), and the owner could already compose a multi-car grant at invite time via CreateShareInviteRequest.vehicleIds — so what this removes is the second redemption, not the grantee's say. The grantee keeps every exit they had. A COPY, NOT A COMPOSITION: `label`, `permission`, `allowRides` and the suspended state all come from the source row and are NOT settable here — offering them would let a caller create a grant that disagrees with the one it claims to extend, and PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId} already edits either row afterwards, per vehicle. A SUSPENDED source produces a SUSPENDED grant: a pause is the owner's own reversible state so it does not block the extend, but copying it live would be a way to undo a suspension without lifting it. STRICTLY DECODED — additionalProperties:false is ENFORCED by the server here, unlike PatchShareInviteRequest where unknown keys are ignored: this body has exactly one required field, so a typo'd key means the request names no share at all, and failing loudly is the only reading that cannot look like success. The 201 response is the NEW ShareInvite — an accepted row on the path vehicle, carrying `allowRides`/`suspended` and the derived `permission`, and carrying neither `code` nor `shareUrl` nor `expiresAt`. Errors: 400 invalid_request (malformed body, unknown key, missing or blank shareId); 401 auth_failed; 403 vehicle_not_owned (the path vehicle is not the caller's); 404 not_found — the path vehicle does not exist, OR the source share is missing / another owner's / still pending / a revoked tombstone, all four INDISTINGUISHABLE so the endpoint cannot be used to probe other people's invite ids; 409 conflict with `subCode: already_shared` when that person already holds a live grant on the target, which is also the answer when the source grant is already on the target vehicle because that IS the already-shared case. Effectively idempotent: a retry answers 409 already_shared rather than stacking a second row, and a client may treat that as success.

shareId.description: The `inviteId` of an ACCEPTED grant belonging to the caller, on a DIFFERENT vehicle they own — i.e. a ShareInvite with status 'accepted' from any GET /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites listing of the caller's other cars. An opaque server-generated cuid; the client never constructs one. A `pending` invite is NOT a valid source and answers 404: nobody has redeemed it, so there is no grantee to extend the share to.

ShareInvite.title: ShareInvite
ShareInvite.description: One owner→recipient sharing grant for ONE vehicle, in either of its two wire-visible lives: an unredeemed invite (status 'pending', carrying the redeemable `code`) or an accepted grant (status 'accepted', the viewer row, carrying the editable `allowRides` / `suspended` flags MYR-369 added). Backed by one `go_vehicle_shares` row (Go-owned, CG-DL-9). Owner-facing ONLY — this object is returned to the vehicle's owner from the invite endpoints and is never delivered to the invited party, who sees only RedeemShareInviteResponse at redemption time and thereafter a `role: 'viewer'` row in their own GET /api/vehicles. Drives the owner's sharing screen rows (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx InvitesScreen Viewers/Pending sections, jsx:1296-1330) and their Resend / Cancel / Revoke actions. Codes, NOT emails: MyRoboTaxi has no email infrastructure and riders are Apple-native, so the owner sends the minted `code` out-of-band through the iOS system share sheet.

inviteId.description: Opaque database identifier for this invite row (the `go_vehicle_shares` id). Path parameter for the single-invite endpoints — DELETE /api/invites/{inviteId} (cancel a pending invite / revoke an accepted grant) and POST /api/invites/{inviteId}/resend. Stable across a resend: resending re-mints the `code` and resets `expiresAt` on the SAME row, so the id a client is holding stays valid. A multi-vehicle invite mints N rows sharing ONE code, so N distinct inviteIds exist for that one code — cancelling one of them affects only that vehicle.

vehicleId.description: Vehicle cuid this invite grants access to — matches VehicleState.vehicleId / VehicleSummary.vehicleId. Always the vehicle in the request path for the list/create endpoints. Exactly one vehicle per row: a multi-vehicle invite is N rows, one per vehicle, sharing a single code (see CreateShareInviteRequest.vehicleIds).

label.description: OWNER-TYPED display name for the recipient — what the owner calls this person ('Mira Chen', 'Mom', 'Roommate'), captured in the send-invite sheet and echoed on the invite/viewer row (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx InvitesScreen row name, jsx:1301,1325). NOT AN EMAIL ADDRESS and not an identity: this contract is code-based, there is no email infrastructure, and the label is never matched against, resolved to, or validated as any account — it is a free-form owner-side memo for their own list. It is therefore NOT overwritten at redemption: after a rider accepts, the row keeps the label the owner typed, not the redeemer's account name. As of MYR-581 the redeemer's ACTUAL name arrives beside it as `acceptedByName` on accepted rows — this field is unchanged in every respect, but it is no longer the only thing an owner has to go on, and a consumer SHOULD prefer `acceptedByName` where present. P1 — a person's name, log-redacted.

permission.description: ON A PENDING ROW: the preset the owner chose in the send-invite sheet's Access step, which redemption maps onto the accepted grant's flags ('rides' → allowRides true, anything else → false). ON AN ACCEPTED ROW: DERIVED from the flags on every read (allowRides → 'rides', otherwise 'live'), NOT a stored tier — see SharePermission for the full retirement note. It is therefore no longer fixed for the life of the row: a PATCH that flips `allowRides` flips this value with it, which is the visible signal to a pre-MYR-369 client that the grant changed. Consumers that understand `allowRides` MUST prefer it; this field is the compatibility projection. Never carries 'live_history' on any response as of MYR-369.

allowRides.description: Whether this viewer may request rides in the vehicle — the per-grant, OWNER-EDITABLE capability that replaced the fixed 'rides' tier (MYR-369). True means they may create a ride request against this car as a rider who is not its owner; false means they see the car (catalog row, snapshot, live WebSocket) but the ride-request path answers 403 `vehicle_not_owned`. ACCEPTED ROWS ONLY: the key is OMITTED while `status` is 'pending', because a pending invite has no grant yet — its eventual value is decided at redemption by mapping the invite's `permission` preset. OPTIONAL for forward/backward compat: absence on an accepted row means the server predates MYR-369, and a consumer MUST then fall back to reading `permission` ('rides' → treat as true), never to assuming either value. NOT INDEPENDENT OF SUSPENSION — `allowRides: true` on a grant whose `suspended` is true grants NOTHING, because suspension gates everything; the flag describes what the grant would allow once active, so a client rendering the owner's controls shows the ride toggle in its stored position even while the grant is suspended, but MUST NOT present the viewer as able to ride. UI-AFFORDANCE HINT ONLY on the viewer side: the server independently enforces the gate on every ride create, owner accept, and reservation dispatch, so a client that ignores this field cannot escalate. Editable in place via PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId}. P0 — an authorization capability, the same tier as `permission`.

suspended.description: Whether this grant is currently SUSPENDED — the owner's reversible pause on one viewer's access to one vehicle (MYR-369), backed by `go_vehicle_shares.suspended_at`. SUSPENSION GATES EVERYTHING, and that is a server-enforced INVARIANT, not a UI convention: a suspended grant is excluded from the viewer's access set entirely, so the vehicle disappears from their GET /api/vehicles, the REST snapshot answers as if they had no grant, the WebSocket subscription is refused, and every drives and rides path dies with it. No capability flag survives it — `allowRides: true` on a suspended grant allows nothing. Restoring (`suspended: false`) returns exactly the capabilities the row already carried; nothing is re-derived and nothing is lost. ACCEPTED ROWS ONLY: OMITTED while `status` is 'pending', where there is no access to suspend. OPTIONAL for compat: absence on an accepted row means the server predates MYR-369 and MUST be read as NOT suspended (false) — absence is never suspension. HOW IT DIFFERS FROM REVOKE: DELETE /api/invites/{inviteId} tombstones the row permanently and the viewer can only return through a fresh invite; suspension keeps the row, keeps its flags, and is one PATCH away from being undone. A SUSPENDED GRANT STILL SERIALIZES on the owner's own §7.5.2 listing — that is the whole point, the owner has to be able to see and un-suspend it — but it produces NO row anywhere on the viewer's own surfaces. P0 — an authorization state.

status.description: Wire lifecycle of this invite row. 'pending' — minted, not yet redeemed; the row carries a live `code` and an `expiresAt`, and the owner's screen lists it under 'Pending' with Resend / Cancel actions. 'accepted' — some rider redeemed the code; the row is now a live viewer grant, carries `acceptedAt`, no longer carries `code`, and the owner's screen lists it under 'Viewers' with a Revoke action. There is deliberately NO 'revoked' member: the server keeps revoked rows as tombstones (status 'revoked' in `go_vehicle_shares`) for audit, but NEVER serializes them — a revoked row vanishes from ShareInviteListResponse instead of appearing with a dead status. Consumers therefore never need to filter this enum, and a Swift/TS client that renders every returned row is correct by construction. Expiry is likewise NOT a status: an expired invite stays 'pending' on the wire (its `expiresAt` is in the past) and simply stops redeeming — the redeem endpoint answers 404 for expired and invalid codes alike.

code.description: The 6-character redemption code the owner shares out-of-band (iOS system share sheet). Uppercase A-Z and 0-9 only — a 36^6 (~2.2 billion) space, which is why the redeem endpoint is rate-limited server-side. OWNER-FACING AND PRESENT ONLY WHILE `status` IS 'pending': the key is OMITTED on every accepted row, so a client MUST NOT expect to re-read the code of a grant that has already been redeemed. Server-minted, never client-supplied. A resend (POST /api/invites/{inviteId}/resend) mints a NEW code and invalidates the previous one. One code may back N rows when the owner invited across multiple vehicles at once — redeeming it grants all N in one atomic operation. Clients MUST send it back verbatim (the entry field upper-cases input and strips non-alphanumerics — ios-app design/app/onboarding.jsx InviteCodeFlow onChange, jsx:428-432). P1 — a live bearer credential for vehicle access: never log it, never put it in an error message, never expose it on any non-owner surface.

shareUrl.description: The COMPLETE signed join link for this invite — what the owner actually hands out through the iOS system share sheet, instead of dictating six characters (MYR-368). Shape, with the parameters in this ORDER: `https://myrobotaxi.app/join/{code}?k={keyId}.{expUnix}.{sigBase64url}&from={ownerFirstName}&to={recipientFirstName}`. PRESENT EXACTLY WHERE `code` IS PRESENT — pending rows only, omitted on every accepted row — and it CONTAINS the code, so it inherits the code's whole handling rule: P1, a live bearer credential, never logged, never in an error envelope, never on a non-owner surface. Clients SHOULD prefer this over hand-assembling a URL from `code`: `k` is an Ed25519 signature the web join shell verifies STATICALLY against a compiled-in public key, with no database and no server round trip, so an unsigned, forged, or tampered link is bounced at the shell without ever reaching an endpoint that could act as a code oracle. `k` has three dot-separated parts: a one-character KEY ID ('1' today, present so a future key rotation can serve both keys at once rather than invalidating every link in flight), the expiry as UNIX SECONDS, and base64url (unpadded, RFC 4648 §5) of the 64-byte signature. CANONICAL SIGNED PAYLOAD — the exact ASCII string a verifier must reconstruct: `join:{code}:{expUnix}:{from}:{to}`, five colon-separated fields, always four colons, using the SANITIZED name values and the EMPTY STRING for a name the URL omits. Every value the link carries is therefore covered by the one signature: the code, the expiry, and BOTH DISPLAY NAMES, so somebody holding a genuine link cannot rewrite `from` to a name the recipient would trust. NAME SANITIZATION (server-side, and what a verifier re-derives from the query as-is): `from` is the owner's resolved display name and `to` is this row's owner-typed `label`; each is reduced to its FIRST whitespace-separated token, stripped to ASCII letters only ([A-Za-z]), and capped at 20 characters — and when nothing survives, the PARAMETER IS OMITTED ENTIRELY rather than emitted empty, and its payload field is the empty string. Accented and non-Latin names therefore lose characters or drop out; a consumer MUST render generic copy when a name is absent, never a placeholder built from the code. The expiry in `k` is the same instant as `expiresAt` in a different encoding; a client that finds the two disagreeing MUST trust `expiresAt`, which is the contract's clock. The signature proves the link came from the server, NOT that the invite is still live: a link may verify and be expired, cancelled, or already redeemed. Redemption stays authoritative — the shell hands the code to POST /api/invites/redeem, which is the only thing that decides. A RESEND RE-SIGNS: new code, new expiry, and the names as they read at that moment, so the whole URL changes and the previous link stops redeeming. OPTIONAL for forward-compat: a consumer that finds `code` without `shareUrl` MUST fall back to sharing the bare code.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC instant this invite row was created — the owner's 'sent {ago}' line on the pending row (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx InvitesScreen, jsx:1326). NOT reset by a resend: a resend re-mints `code` and pushes out `expiresAt` but leaves createdAt at the original send.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC instant after which the `code` stops redeeming — 7 days from mint. PENDING ROWS ONLY: the key is OMITTED on accepted rows (an accepted grant does not expire; ending it is a revoke). Reset forward by a resend. Passing this instant does NOT change `status` — the row stays 'pending' with an expiresAt in the past until the owner cancels or resends it, so consumers that want an 'Expired' affordance MUST derive it by comparing this value to the current time. Also OPTIONAL for forward-compat: absence on a pending row means the server did not supply an expiry, which consumers MUST render as 'no expiry shown', NEVER as expired.

acceptedAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC instant a rider redeemed the code and this row became a live viewer grant. OPTIONAL on the wire: the key is OMITTED while `status` is 'pending', and is never cleared afterwards. The redeeming account's IDENTIFIER is deliberately NOT on this object — the redeemer's user id lives server-side in `go_vehicle_shares.accepted_by_user_id` (go_users id space) and is not part of the owner-facing wire shape. Since MYR-581 the redeemer's NAME is: see `acceptedByName`, which is the resolved projection of that same id and supersedes this field's former instruction to identify the person by the `label`.

acceptedByName.description: The CONFIRMED display FIRST NAME of the account that REDEEMED this invite (MYR-581, contracts v0.37.0; confirmation-gated by MYR-583 on the GRANTEE's own confirmation, the mirror of VehicleSummary.ownerFirstName) — the name the shared user themselves entered at signup, resolved by the platform's three-source identity ladder (Prisma "User".name → the Apple first-consent name in go_identity_apple → go_users) and reduced to its first whitespace-separated token, the same resolution and the same reduction behind `RideRequest.requesterName`, `RedeemShareInviteResponse.ownerFirstName` and `VehicleSummary.ownerFirstName`. THIS IS THE CORRECTION TO `label`, NOT A DUPLICATE OF IT: `label` is the owner's own memo about who they MEANT to invite, typed in the send-invite sheet before anybody redeemed anything and never resolved against an account — so a code forwarded to somebody else leaves an accepted row labelled with the wrong person's name, and until this field the owner's Share tab had no way to say who actually holds the grant. An owner deciding whether to revoke or suspend needs the second, not the first. Consumers SHOULD render this in preference to `label` on accepted rows, and fall back to `label` when it is absent. OPTIONAL: the key is OMITTED while `status` is 'pending' (nobody has accepted, so there is nobody to name), on an accepted row whose account has no resolvable name in any identity source, and on an accepted row whose account has a name it never confirmed (MYR-583). Those three are deliberately INDISTINGUISHABLE — `status` already separates them, and a second sentinel would be a state with no copy. FIRST NAMES ONLY, the P1 counterparty policy: this is a grantee's name delivered to the owner, and it gets exactly the treatment the owner's name gets when it is delivered to the grantee. P1 — never logged. OWNER-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: the viewer role has no entry in the Invite mask resource at all, and a viewer must never be able to enumerate the other people an owner has shared with.

CreateShareInviteRequest.title: CreateShareInviteRequest
CreateShareInviteRequest.description: Request body for POST /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites — what the owner's send-invite sheet submits (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx InvitesScreen send flow, jsx:1264-1278). Deliberately a strict subset of ShareInvite: the owner is the authenticated JWT sub (never client-supplied), and inviteId / status / code / createdAt / expiresAt are all server-assigned. The caller MUST own the path vehicle. The server responds 201 Created with a single ShareInvite — see `vehicleIds` for exactly WHICH invite that is on a multi-vehicle create.

label.description: Owner-typed recipient name for the invite — see ShareInvite.label. Free-form and NOT an email: it is a memo for the owner's own list, never resolved to an account. Applied identically to every row a multi-vehicle create mints. P1 — a person's name.

permission.description: The INVITE-TIME PRESET deciding what the grant gets when somebody redeems this code: 'rides' redeems to allowRides true, 'live' redeems to allowRides false. Applied identically to every row a multi-vehicle create mints; per-vehicle presets are NOT expressible at create time — but the capabilities they produce ARE editable per vehicle afterwards through PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId} (MYR-369), which is where a per-vehicle difference is now expressed. 'live_history' IS STILL ACCEPTED so an installed client's send-invite sheet does not start failing, but the server PERSISTS AND REDEEMS IT AS 'live' — the tier is retired (see SharePermission) and the invite that comes back carries `permission: "live"`. A client MUST therefore read the created row's `permission` rather than assume the value it sent round-trips. The design collects this in the sheet's Access step (ios-app design/app/screens.jsx SHARE_ACCESS, jsx:1235-1239).

vehicleIds.description: MULTI-VEHICLE INVITE: the full set of vehicles this one invite should grant, from the sheet's 'select one or more' vehicle multi-select (design/Handoff for Claude Code.md §send-invite sheet). OPTIONAL — omit it for the ordinary single-vehicle case, which is exactly equivalent to sending `[<path vehicleId>]`. WHEN PRESENT IT MUST INCLUDE THE PATH VEHICLE; a set that omits the vehicle in the URL is rejected 400 `invalid_request`, because the path vehicle is what authorizes the call. Every id MUST be a vehicle the caller owns (otherwise 403 `permission_denied`); an empty array is rejected 400 `invalid_request`. The server creates ONE `go_vehicle_shares` ROW PER VEHICLE, all sharing a SINGLE `code`, so one redemption grants the whole set atomically — but the 201 RESPONSE IS A SINGLE ShareInvite: the row for the PATH VEHICLE. The sibling rows are not returned; the client learns them by listing each vehicle's invites, and the shared `code` on the returned row is the one to hand out for all of them. Cancelling one row (DELETE /api/invites/{inviteId}) removes only that vehicle from the grant set.

items.description: Vehicle cuid owned by the caller — same id space as VehicleSummary.vehicleId.

RedeemShareInviteRequest.title: RedeemShareInviteRequest
RedeemShareInviteRequest.description: Request body for POST /api/invites/redeem — the rider-side join, submitted by the iOS invite-code screen once six characters are entered (ios-app design/app/onboarding.jsx InviteCodeFlow submit, jsx:419-434). Authenticated: the redeeming account is the JWT sub and is never client-supplied. ATOMIC and IDEMPOTENT PER REDEEMER — re-submitting a code the same account already redeemed returns 200 with the same RedeemShareInviteResponse rather than minting a second grant (enforced by the partial-unique index over one accepted grant per (vehicle, user)), so a retried request after a dropped response is safe. RATE-LIMITED server-side (429 `rate_limited`): the code space is only 36^6, so brute-force enumeration is a real threat.

code.description: The 6-character invite code the owner shared, uppercase A-Z / 0-9 — see ShareInvite.code. Clients MUST normalize before sending exactly as the design's entry field does: upper-case and strip everything outside [A-Z0-9] (ios-app design/app/onboarding.jsx, jsx:428-432). A code that is unknown, already-consumed for a different account, or past its `expiresAt` all answer 404 `not_found` with an INDISTINGUISHABLE body — the server deliberately does not tell an enumerating caller which of those it hit. An OWNER redeeming their OWN vehicle's code answers 409 `conflict` (you cannot become a viewer of a car you already own). A malformed code — wrong length or illegal characters — is 400 `invalid_request`. P1 — a live bearer credential: never log it and never echo it in an error message.

RedeemShareInviteResponse.title: RedeemShareInviteResponse
RedeemShareInviteResponse.description: 200 response body for POST /api/invites/redeem — everything the rider's success screen needs to render without a second round-trip (ios-app design/app/onboarding.jsx JoinedSuccess: "You can now ride in {owner}'s Tesla" plus the vehicle card, jsx:493-527). This is the ONLY sharing payload the invited party ever sees: ShareInvite is owner-facing and is never returned here (it would leak the owner-typed `label` and the still-live `code`). Returned identically on an idempotent re-redeem by the same account.

ownerFirstName.description: The sharing owner's FIRST NAME only — the '{owner}' in "You can now ride in {owner}'s Tesla" and in the success card's "{owner}'s {vehicle name}" line (ios-app design/app/onboarding.jsx JoinedSuccess, jsx:509,519). Server-derived from the owner's identity with the same ladder RideRequest.requesterName uses: first name -> email local-part -> a generic fallback. DELIBERATELY NARROW: first name only, no surname, no email, no user id — a redeemer learns the minimum needed to recognize whose car they just joined. Always present (the fallback guarantees a non-empty string), so consumers never need an absent-name branch. P1 — a person's name, log-redacted.

vehicles.description: The vehicles this redemption granted, as ordinary VehicleSummary rows identical in shape to GET /api/vehicles — so the client can render the success card and seed its catalog from one response. Always present and NEVER empty: a redemption that granted nothing would have answered 404 or 409 instead. Length > 1 when the owner sent a multi-vehicle invite (N rows, one code). Every row carries `role: 'viewer'` and a `sharePermission` DERIVED from the flags the redemption just wrote (MYR-369): the invite's `permission` preset maps to those flags, so a 'rides' invite yields 'rides' here and every other preset — including a legacy 'live_history' one — yields 'live'. On an idempotent re-redeem the same rows are returned. Rows are the VIEWER-MASKED projection — the same masking GET /api/vehicles applies to a viewer-merged row, with no owner-only fields.
